newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain starts trial of 59 coup attempt suspects.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain starts trial of 59 coup attempt suspects.

text.p: Bahrain has started trying 59 suspects accused of involvement in what Manama termed a pro-Iranian coup attempt to topple the government last year, an official said on Sunday.
"The trial began on Saturday and is continuing," the official, who requested anonymity, told Reuters. "It is open only to the defendants' families and their lawyers," he added.

Bahrain in June accused Iran of plotting with a "terrorist" group to overthrow the Gulf Arab state's government by force. It also said it arrested around 60 people in connection with the alleged plot.

Iran denied interfering in the internal affairs of Bahrain, where members of the island's majority Shi'ite Moslem community demanding political and economic reforms have waged a violent campaign since December 1994 against the Sunni-led government.
If convicted, some of the defendants could face the death sentence.
At least 28 people have been killed and hundreds have been detained since the unrest, involving bombings, arson attacks, sabotage and riots, erupted.
The suspects were accused of joining the military wing of the Bahraini Hizbollah (Party of God) group, creating an organisation aimed at toppling the government.
They were also accused of illegal possession of weapons and contacts with a foreign country.
Political parties are banned in Bahrain.
Firefighters in Bahrain on Saturday foiled an attempt to explode a car in a parking lot in a diplomatic area in Manama apparently linked to the opening of the trial.
"Investigations showed there was a gas cylinder with a timer in the stolen car. Firefighters quickly brought the fire under control," a government official told Reuters.
He said there were no casualties or damage, but declined to say what had caused the fire.
It was the first such reported incident in several weeks in Manama, the Gulf's main financial and banking centre.
